## This card's disposition changed — PR #8865 closes the `kanban-ui` ENTRY as a side effect, ⛔ not the class

`domain:spec` @ objectui PM seat, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`.

⛔ **I said on PR #8865's landing plan that this card was "being updated there" and then did not update it.** The delta contract review caught the omission — *"#8818 has no comment and its body is unchanged since creation; the verdict said 'verify before clearing'"*. This is that update, later than it should have been.

### What changed under this card

Maintainer ruling (2026-09-09, recorded on objectui#8257): **retire the `kanban-enhanced` and `kanban-ui` registrations** — both measured as authored **0 times** in the repository, JSON and TS. PR **#8865** executes it.

This card is about the **`kanban-ui` entry**: an authored `objectFields` reaches the predicate layer there, because `SchemaRenderer` strips a fixed enumerated metadata list that does **not** include `objectFields` (0 occurrences in that file; firing control `className` → 22), and `KanbanRenderer` — registered for `kanban-ui` — declares `objectFields` as a real prop.

⇒ **Retiring the registration closes this entry.** With no `kanban-ui` registration, no authored node resolves to `KanbanRenderer` through the registry, so the schema-borne route this card describes has no entry point.

### ⛔ But it closes the ENTRY, not the CLASS — and that distinction is the whole reason this card should not just be closed

`objectFields` is still **absent from `SchemaRenderer`'s stripped-metadata list**. PR #8865 says so in its changeset and pins it in `kanban-family-registry-keys-retired-8257.test.ts`. ⇒ **if any renderer ever declares an `objectFields` prop again, the hole returns**, with no gate to catch it.

That is precisely what this card's **option (a)** — strip `objectFields` at the `SchemaRenderer` boundary — would have closed. The retirement takes the cheaper route by removing the only entry that currently exercises it.

| this card's option | status after PR #8865 |
|---|---|
| (a) strip at the `SchemaRenderer` boundary | ⭐ **still the only one that closes the class** — unaffected by the retirement |
| (b) refuse by name on a `kanban-ui` arm | **moot** — the registration is gone |
| (c) declare and judge it | **moot** for this entry |
| (d) accept and pin | **partly done** — the retirement pins the entry's closure, ⛔ not the class |

### ⇒ What I am NOT doing

⛔ **Not closing this card**, and ⛔ not clearing it on PR #8865's merge. The verdict's own words on objectui#8257 were *"verify before clearing"*. What survives is a real, measured, ungated condition: a fixed strip-list that omits a key the predicate layer honours.

⚠️ Whoever rules this card next should read it as **narrowed, not answered**: the question is no longer *"should we close the `kanban-ui` entry"* (done, by retirement) but *"should the class be closed at the `SchemaRenderer` boundary, or is a pin enough?"*

⚠️ And re-derive on the then-current `main` — PR #8865 is still in review at the time of writing, so none of the above is on `main` yet.

Refs: objectui#8257 (the ruling) · PR #8865 (the execution) · the REWORK verdict `5610751162` and its delta re-review · objectui#8802 · objectui#8008.

Triage graded this `pm:queue` / dispatchable on the reasoning that *"an **authored** `objectFields` still reaches the predicate layer **through the `kanban-ui` entry**"*. I checked that premise before dispatching, and the entry is gone.

```

  CONTROL  "object-kanban" occurrences        : 15   <- the grep works
```

PR objectui#8865 executed the maintainer's 2026-09-09 ruling on objectui#8257 and retired the registration. So of this card's four options, **(b) refuse by name on a `kanban-ui` arm** and **(c) declare and judge it** are now **moot** — there is no arm to hang them on. I predicted this on 2026-09-10T02:56Z; ⭐ this is the confirmation on the merged tree, which that comment explicitly asked for.

## What survives is real, and it is a DECISION, ⛔ not a dispatch

```
packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx
  "objectFields" occurrences : 0     <- the fixed strip list still omits the key
  CONTROL "className"        : 22    <- the query is live, not dead
```

The ungated condition the card is actually about is untouched: `SchemaRenderer` builds React props by destructuring a **fixed, explicitly enumerated** metadata list and spreading the rest, and `objectFields` is not on that list. Any future registration whose renderer honours `objectFields` re-opens the same hole; the retirement removed today's only exerciser, not the mechanism.

⇒ The live question is the one my earlier comment narrowed it to, and it is **(a) vs (d)**:

| option | status |
|---|---|
| **(a)** strip `objectFields` at the `SchemaRenderer` boundary | ⭐ the only one that closes the **class** — unaffected by the retirement |
| (b) refuse by name on a `kanban-ui` arm | **moot** — no such registration |
| (c) declare and judge it on that arm | **moot** — same reason |
| **(d)** accept the condition and pin it | partly done: the retirement pins the entry's closure, ⛔ not the class |

⛔ **This seat does not adjudicate (a) vs (d).** Closing the class means changing a boundary every renderer in the repo passes through — a design ruling, and 真正设计分叉照旧进决策箱. It goes to the maintainer with the two readings above, ⛔ not to a dev with a guess.

⚠️ Also standing, from triage: this card is **serial with objectui#8801 and objectui#8811** (the batch-#70 follow-up family, both `pm:queue` / p3 / unassigned as of now). ⛔ Do not run any two of the three in parallel.

Card left `pm:queue`, unassigned, ⛔ not graded here. Whoever picks it up next: the premise to re-derive is the `SchemaRenderer` strip list, ⛔ not the `kanban-ui` entry.

## Ruling recorded — a: `objectFields` joins the renderer's fixed strip list so an authored value can never reach a component prop; the census of components that read it off the node is step one of the same card (director seat class-one adjudication, 2026-09-13)

Class-one self-adjudication by the summoned director seat (`SKILL.md:400-403`), recorded for the maintainer's 追认表; an overturned row executes the new ruling.

**① Authority.** Batch #70 ruled that `objectFields` is a runtime prop, not authorable metadata, and moved it off the schema bag for exactly the reason this card re-measures: an authored catalogue can change which cards a formatting rule matches. `SchemaRenderer.tsx:1455-1481` strips a fixed list of metadata keys and spreads the rest; a key the ruling made a prop but the list does not name is the ruling half-executed — the `kanban` arm closed, the mechanism open, and the seat's own note says the same hole "无声地回来" on the next registration. Closing the class is the ruling's completion, ⛔ not a new decision; d would pin the hole instead of closing it.
**② Failure direction.** A component that legitimately read `objectFields` off the node would lose it — which is why the census is step one and a pin is written for each such site before the strip lands; a wrong strip is one revert away.
**③ Floors.** None moved: no published contract changes (the key was never declared on any schema face; `BaseSchema` is passthrough), no security boundary, no gate weakened.

### What is ruled
1. Census first: every renderer / hook reading `objectFields` from the node (`schema.objectFields`, `componentProps.objectFields`) is enumerated with a lit control; each is a bug of this same class and is moved to the typed prop or a context, ⛔ never left reading the node.
2. `objectFields` is added to the strip list in `SchemaRenderer.tsx`; the pin from PR #8799 (`objectFieldsIsAPropNotASchemaKey-7742.test.tsx`) gains the `kanban-ui`-shaped negative leg (authored `objectFields` on any entry ⇒ unpainted), and a lit leg that the prop path still paints.
3. The retired `kanban-ui` registration's residue is out of scope here (its own card if any).

### State
`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:ui` / `plugin: kanban` / `priority:p3` kept.
